memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria: Patient reports daily hives, mild angioedema, worse in evenings. Currently on levocetirizine 5 mg OD and cetirizine 10 mg HS with partial relief. Status: active. Plan: Continue antihistamines, add fexofenadine 120 mg BD if needed, monitor eosinophils.
- Atrial fibrillation: Asymptomatic, on apixaban 5 mg BD and bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. Rate controlled. Status: active. Plan: Continue anticoagulation, check INR if warfarin considered, ECG today.
- Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep, uses melatonin 3 mg HS with limited benefit. Status: active. Plan: Add trazodone 50 mg HS, review sleep hygiene.
Due: HbA1c not indicated; next review in 3 months.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: ECG: Rhythm irregularly irregular with absent P waves, ventricular rate 78 bpm. No ST-T changes. Consistent with atrial fibrillation, controlled ventricular response.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Rao, Cardiology, Vikram Hospital, for opinion on long-term anticoagulation strategy in atrial fibrillation and assessment of thromboembolic risk. Please advise on suitability of warfarin vs continued apixaban, and need for echocardiogram.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: "Doctor, my hives have been worse the past week, especially at night, and I'm still struggling to sleep despite melatonin. I feel tired during the day."

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for follow-up with Dr Karthik Hegde (D04) on 2025-07-10 at 10:30 AM. Reason: review of urticaria, atrial fibrillation medications, and insomnia treatment.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria: Patient reports reduced hive frequency, still occasional nocturnal wheals. Eosinophils normal. Status: improving. Plan: Continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD, add cetirizine 10 mg HS only if breakthrough, consider short course of prednisolone 10 mg OD for 3 days if severe flare.
- Atrial fibrillation: Patient reports no palpitations. On apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. Discussed warfarin option; patient prefers to stay on apixaban. Status: stable. Plan: Continue apixaban, check renal function annually.
- Insomnia: Sleep onset improved with trazodone 50 mg HS, reports 6 hours sleep. Status: improved. Plan: Continue trazodone, melatonin as needed, advise sleep hygiene.
Due: Next review in 3 months (Oct 2025).

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Cardiology opinion: Patient's atrial fibrillation is paroxysmal, well-controlled on apixaban and bisoprolol. Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular size, mild left atrial enlargement, EF 60%. No valvular disease. Recommend continuation of apixaban 5 mg BD, maintain bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. No need to switch to warfarin unless bleeding or adherence issues. Annual echocardiogram advised.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Chronic urticaria: Patient reports occasional mild wheals, mostly controlled with levocetirizine; no rescue cetirizine needed in past month. Status: well-controlled. Plan: Continue levocetirizine 5 mg OD, consider trial off cetirizine.
- Atrial fibrillation: No symptoms, apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. Rate controlled. Status: stable. Plan: Continue same, repeat INR not needed, annual lipid profile done.
- Insomnia: Sleep quality good, trazodone 50 mg HS nightly, melatonin prn. Status: controlled. Plan: Continue current regimen, review in 6 months.
Due: Next review in 6 months (Apr 2027) – outside current window; advise patient to return if symptoms change.
